/-!
# Erdős Problem 233

*References:*
  - [erdosproblems.com/233](https://www.erdosproblems.com/233)
  - [A74741](https://oeis.org/A74741)
  - [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cram%C3%A9r%27s_conjecture)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter Real

namespace Erdos233

/--
A conjecture by Heath-Brown:
The sum of squares of the first $N$ gaps between consecutive primes behaves like $N * (log N)^2$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_233 :
    (fun N => ((∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, (primeGap n) ^ 2) : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun N => N * (log N)^2 := by
  sorry

/--
Cramér proved an upper bound of $O(N(\log N)^4)$ conditional on the Riemann hypothesis.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_233.variants.upper_bound (h : RiemannHypothesis) :
    (fun N => ((∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, (primeGap n) ^ 2) : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun N => N * (log N)^4 := by
  sorry

/--
The prime number theorem immediately implies a lower bound of $\gg N(\log N)^2$ for the sum of
squares of gaps between consecutive primes.

Formal proof linked here provided by AlphaProof.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at "https://github.com/mzhorvath1/formal-conjectures/blob/032848c62fdf4c422bb0ee6663dc8d009d456c2c/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/233.lean#L57"]
theorem erdos_233.variants.lower_bound :
    (fun (N : ℕ) => N * (log N)^2) =O[atTop]
    (fun N => ((∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, (primeGap n) ^ 2) : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

end Erdos233

reformulations.difference: The Lean bound counts the first N prime gaps and uses N(log N)^4. The standard prime-cutoff formulation, recorded in Heath-Brown's introduction, sums over p_n ≤ x and uses x(log x)^3.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Write S(N)=∑_{n=1}^N(p_{n+1}−p_n)^2 and T(x)=∑_{p_n≤x}(p_{n+1}−p_n)^2. Then T(x)=S(π(x)). The prime number theorem gives π(x)(log π(x))^4 ∼ x(log x)^3, yielding the cutoff bound from the Lean bound. Conversely, take x=p_N: π(p_N)=N and p_N(log p_N)^3 ∼ N(log N)^4. Thus the Big-O statements are equivalent, with the same RH hypothesis.

could_not_verify: Erdos233.erdos_233: Could not complete the exact comparison with the current statement and remarks at https://www.erdosproblems.com/233. The page repeatedly returned a Cloudflare challenge despite descriptive User-Agent headers, and alternate retrieval/archive attempts did not recover it. Erdős's original 1955 upper-bound conjecture matches the Lean statement, but OEIS and Heath-Brown also record a strictly stronger asymptotic with leading constant 2. Without the problem page, I cannot definitively verify which strength its current main statement selects; this uncertainty is not reported as a defect.
review.notes: Checked all three declarations, including elaborated types, indexing, casts, Big-O direction, RH's definition, and boundary cases. Nat.nth Prime is zero-indexed and strictly increasing, so primeGap uses genuine nontruncated differences. Lean verified the first four gaps and sums; an independent finite computation matched OEIS's first ten partial sums. N=0 and N=1 cause no problem because the bounds are eventual on the nontrivial filter atTop on ℕ. Reproduced the linked lower-bound proof in /workspace/review/check_lower_proof.lean, updating renamed Mathlib lemmas; #print axioms reports only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. Also proved the explicit eventual-inequality interpretations and the equivalence of the main upper bound with a two-sided Theta bound using that independently checked lower bound. This does not establish equivalence with the stronger asymptotic S(N) ∼ 2N(log N)^2 in OEIS/Heath-Brown. The mathematical status database still records problem 233 as open; no consulted evidence contradicts the two solved-variant tags.
